1.sahih_international: The Hour has come near, and the moon has split [in two].
1.pickthall: The hour drew nigh and the moon was rent in twain.
1.yusuf_ali: The Hour (of Judgment) is nigh, and the moon is cleft asunder.
1.shakir: The hour drew nigh and the moon did rend asunder.
1.muhammad_sarwar: The Hour of Doom is drawing near and the moon is rent asunder.
1.mohsin_khan: The Hour has drawn near, and the moon has been cleft asunder (the people of Makkah requested Prophet Muhammad SAW to show them a miracle, so he showed them the splitting of the moon).
1.arberry: The Hour has drawn nigh: the moon is split.

2.sahih_international: And if they see a miracle, they turn away and say, "Passing magic."
2.pickthall: And if they behold a portent they turn away and say: Prolonged illusion.
2.yusuf_ali: But if they see a Sign, they turn away, and say, "This is (but) transient magic."
2.shakir: And if they see a miracle they turn aside and say: Transient magic.
2.muhammad_sarwar: Whenever they see a miracle, they turn away from it and say, "This is just a powerful magic".
2.mohsin_khan: And if they see a sign, they turn away, and say: "This is continuous magic."
2.arberry: Yet if they see a sign they turn away, and they say 'A continuous sorcery!'

3.sahih_international: And they denied and followed their inclinations. But for every matter is a [time of] settlement.
3.pickthall: They denied (the Truth) and followed their own lusts. Yet everything will come to a decision
3.yusuf_ali: They reject (the warning) and follow their (own) lusts but every matter has its appointed time.
3.shakir: And they call (it) a lie, and follow their low desires; and every affair has its appointed term.
3.muhammad_sarwar: They have rejected it and have followed their own desires, but all matters will be settled (by God).
3.mohsin_khan: They belied (the Verses of Allah, this Quran), and followed their own lusts. And every matter will be settled [according to the kind of deeds (for the doer of good deeds, his deeds will take him to Paradise, and similarly evil deeds will take their doers to Hell)].
3.arberry: They have cried lies, and followed their caprices; but every matter is settled.

4.sahih_international: And there has already come to them of information that in which there is deterrence -
4.pickthall: And surely there hath come unto them news whereof the purport should deter,
4.yusuf_ali: There have already come to them Recitals wherein there is (enough) to check (them),
4.shakir: And certainly some narratives have come to them wherein is prevention--
4.muhammad_sarwar: They have certainly received the kind of news in which there is a lesson and strong words of wisdom,
4.mohsin_khan: And indeed there has come to them news (in this Quran) wherein there is (enough warning) to check (them from evil),
4.arberry: And there have come to them such tidings as contain a deterrent --

5.sahih_international: Extensive wisdom - but warning does not avail [them].
5.pickthall: Effective wisdom; but warnings avail not.
5.yusuf_ali: Mature wisdom;- but (the preaching of) Warners profits them not.
5.shakir: Consummate wisdom-- but warnings do not avail;
5.muhammad_sarwar: but the warnings have proved to have no effect on them.
5.mohsin_khan: Perfect wisdom (this Quran), but (the preaching of) warners benefit them not,
5.arberry: a Wisdom far-reaching; yet warnings do not avail.

6.sahih_international: So leave them, [O Muhammad]. The Day the Caller calls to something forbidding,
6.pickthall: So withdraw from them (O Muhammad) on the day when the Summoner summoneth unto a painful thing.
6.yusuf_ali: Therefore, (O Prophet,) turn away from them. The Day that the Caller will call (them) to a terrible affair,
6.shakir: So turn (your) back on them (for) the day when the inviter shall invite them to a hard task,
6.muhammad_sarwar: (Muhammad), leave them alone. On the day when they will be called to a terrible punishment,
6.mohsin_khan: So (O Muhammad SAW) withdraw from them. The Day that the caller will call (them) to a terrible thing.
6.arberry: So turn thou away from them. Upon the day when the Caller shall call unto a horrible thing,

7.sahih_international: Their eyes humbled, they will emerge from the graves as if they were locusts spreading,
7.pickthall: With downcast eyes, they come forth from the graves as they were locusts spread abroad,
7.yusuf_ali: They will come forth,- their eyes humbled - from (their) graves, (torpid) like locusts scattered abroad,
7.shakir: Their eyes cast down, going forth from their graves as if they were scattered locusts,
7.muhammad_sarwar: they will come out of their graves, their eyes cast down, hastening towards their Summoner as locusts rushing about.
7.mohsin_khan: They will come forth, with humbled eyes from (their) graves as if they were locusts spread abroad,
7.arberry: abasing their eyes, they shall come forth from the tombs as if they were scattered grasshoppers,

8.sahih_international: Racing ahead toward the Caller. The disbelievers will say, "This is a difficult Day."
8.pickthall: Hastening toward the summoner; the disbelievers say: This is a hard day.
8.yusuf_ali: Hastening, with eyes transfixed, towards the Caller!- "Hard is this Day!", the Unbelievers will say.
8.shakir: Hastening to the inviter. The unbelievers shall say: This is a hard day.
8.muhammad_sarwar: These disbelievers will say, "This is a hard day".
8.mohsin_khan: Hastening towards the caller, the disbelievers will say: "This is a hard Day."
8.arberry: running with outstretched necks to the Caller. The unbelievers shall say, 'This is a hard day!'

9.sahih_international: The people of Noah denied before them, and they denied Our servant and said, "A madman," and he was repelled.
9.pickthall: The folk of Noah denied before them, yea, they denied Our slave and said: A madman; and he was repulsed.
9.yusuf_ali: Before them the People of Noah rejected (their messenger): they rejected Our servant, and said, "Here is one possessed!", and he was driven out.
9.shakir: Before them the people of Nuh rejected, so they rejected Our servant and called (him) mad, and he was driven away.
9.muhammad_sarwar: The people of Noah, who lived before them, had also rejected (Our guidance). They rejected Our servant and said, "He is an insane person so let us drive him away".
9.mohsin_khan: The people of Nuh (Noah) denied (their Messenger) before them, they rejected Our slave, and said: "A madman!" and he was insolently rebuked and threatened.
9.arberry: The people of Noah cried lies before them; they cried lies to Our servant, and said, 'A man possessed!' And he was rejected.

10.sahih_international: So he invoked his Lord, "Indeed, I am overpowered, so help."
10.pickthall: So he cried unto his Lord, saying: I am vanquished, so give help.
10.yusuf_ali: Then he called on his Lord: "I am one overcome: do Thou then help (me)!"
10.shakir: Therefore he called upon his Lord: I am overcome, come Thou then to help.
10.muhammad_sarwar: Noah prayed, "Lord, help me; I am defeated".
10.mohsin_khan: Then he invoked his Lord (saying): "I have been overcome, so help (me)!"
10.arberry: And so he called unto his Lord, saying, 'I am vanquished; do Thou succour me!'

11.sahih_international: Then We opened the gates of the heaven with rain pouring down
11.pickthall: Then opened We the gates of heaven with pouring water
11.yusuf_ali: So We opened the gates of heaven, with water pouring forth.
11.shakir: So We opened the gates of the cloud with water pouring
11.muhammad_sarwar: We opened the gates of the sky and water started to pour down.
11.mohsin_khan: So We opened the gates of heaven with water pouring forth.
11.arberry: Then We opened the gates of heaven unto water torrential,

12.sahih_international: And caused the earth to burst with springs, and the waters met for a matter already predestined.
12.pickthall: And caused the earth to gush forth springs, so that the waters met for a predestined purpose.
12.yusuf_ali: And We caused the earth to gush forth with springs, so the waters met (and rose) to the extent decreed.
12.shakir: And We made water to flow forth in the land in springs, so the water gathered together according to a measure already ordained.
12.muhammad_sarwar: We caused the earth to burst forth with springs so that the waters could come together for a predestined purpose.
12.mohsin_khan: And We caused the earth to gush forth with springs. So the waters (of the heaven and the earth) met for a matter predestined.
12.arberry: and made the earth to gush with fountains, and the waters met for a matter decreed.

13.sahih_international: And We carried him on a [construction of] planks and nails,
13.pickthall: And We carried him upon a thing of planks and nails,
13.yusuf_ali: But We bore him on an (Ark) made of broad planks and caulked with palm-fibre:
13.shakir: And We bore him on that which was made of planks and nails
13.muhammad_sarwar: We carried him, (Noah), on a vessel built with boards fixed together with nails,
13.mohsin_khan: And We carried him on a (ship) made of planks and nails,
13.arberry: And We bore him upon a well-planked vessel well-caulked

14.sahih_international: Sailing under Our observation as reward for he who had been denied.
14.pickthall: That ran (upon the waters) in Our sight, as a reward for him who was rejected.
14.yusuf_ali: She floats under our eyes (and care): a recompense to one who had been rejected (with scorn)!
14.shakir: Sailing, before Our eyes, a reward for him who was denied.
14.muhammad_sarwar: which floated on the water before Our very eyes. The flood was a recompense for the deeds of the disbelievers.
14.mohsin_khan: Floating under Our Eyes, a reward for him who had been rejected!
14.arberry: running before Our eyes-a recompense for him denied.

15.sahih_international: And We left it as a sign, so is there any who will remember?
15.pickthall: And verily We left it as a token; but is there any that remembereth?
15.yusuf_ali: And We have left this as a Sign (for all time): then is there any that will receive admonition?
15.shakir: And certainly We left it as a sign, but is there anyone who
15.muhammad_sarwar: We made (the story of Noah) as evidence of the Truth. However, is there anyone who would take heed?
15.mohsin_khan: And indeed, We have left this as a sign, then is there any that will remember (or receive admonition)?
15.arberry: And We left it for a sign. Is there any that will remember?

16.sahih_international: And how [severe] were My punishment and warning.
16.pickthall: Then see how (dreadful) was My punishment after My warnings!
16.yusuf_ali: But how (terrible) was My Penalty and My Warning?
16.shakir: How (great) was then My punishment and My warning!
16.muhammad_sarwar: How terrible was My torment and the result of (their disregard) of My warning.
16.mohsin_khan: Then how (terrible) was My Torment and My Warnings?
16.arberry: How then were My chastisement and My warnings?

17.sahih_international: And We have certainly made the Qur'an easy for remembrance, so is there any who will remember?
17.pickthall: And in truth We have made the Qur'an easy to remember; but is there any that remembereth?
17.yusuf_ali: And We have indeed made the Qur'an easy to understand and remember: then is there any that will receive admonition?
17.shakir: And certainly We have made the Quran easy for remembrance, but is there anyone who will mind?
17.muhammad_sarwar: We have made the Quran easy to understand, but is there anyone who would pay attention?
17.mohsin_khan: And We have indeed made the Quran easy to understand and remember, then is there any that will remember (or receive admonition)?
17.arberry: Now We have made the Koran easy for Remembrance. Is there any that will remember?

18.sahih_international: 'Aad denied; and how [severe] were My punishment and warning.
18.pickthall: (The tribe of) A'ad rejected warnings. Then how (dreadful) was My punishment after My warnings.
18.yusuf_ali: The 'Ad (people) (too) rejected (Truth): then how terrible was My Penalty and My Warning?
18.shakir: Ad treated (the truth) as a lie, so how (great) was My punishment and My warning!
18.muhammad_sarwar: The people of `Ad rejected Our guidance. How terrible was My torment and the result (of their disregard) of My warning.
18.mohsin_khan: 'Ad (people) belied (their Prophet, Hud), then how (terrible) was My Torment and My Warnings?
18.arberry: Ad cried lies. How then were My chastisement and My warnings?

19.sahih_international: Indeed, We sent upon them a screaming wind on a day of continuous misfortune,
19.pickthall: Lo! We let loose on them a raging wind on a day of constant calamity,
19.yusuf_ali: For We sent against them a furious wind, on a Day of violent Disaster,
19.shakir: Surely We sent on them a tornado in a day of bitter ill-luck
19.muhammad_sarwar: On an unfortunate day We sent upon them a continuous violent wind
19.mohsin_khan: Verily, We sent against them a furious wind of harsh voice on a day of evil omen and continuous calamity.
19.arberry: We loosed against them a wind clamorous in a day of ill fortune continuous,

20.sahih_international: Extracting the people as if they were trunks of palm trees uprooted.
20.pickthall: Sweeping men away as though they were uprooted trunks of palm-trees.
20.yusuf_ali: Plucking out men as if they were roots of palm-trees torn up (from the ground).
20.shakir: Tearing men away as if they were the trunks of palm-trees torn up.
20.muhammad_sarwar: which hurled people around like uprooted trunks of palm-trees.
20.mohsin_khan: Plucking out men as if they were uprooted stems of date-palms.
20.arberry: plucking up men as if they were stumps of uprooted palm-trees.

21.sahih_international: And how [severe] were My punishment and warning.
21.pickthall: Then see how (dreadful) was My punishment after My warnings!
21.yusuf_ali: Yea, how (terrible) was My Penalty and My Warning!
21.shakir: How (great) was then My punishment and My warning!
21.muhammad_sarwar: How terrible was Our torment and the result of (their disregard) of Our warning.
21.mohsin_khan: Then, how (terrible) was My Torment and My Warnings?
21.arberry: How then were My chastisement and My warnings?

22.sahih_international: And We have certainly made the Qur'an easy for remembrance, so is there any who will remember?
22.pickthall: And in truth We have made the Qur'an easy to remember; but is there any that remembereth?
22.yusuf_ali: But We have indeed made the Qur'an easy to understand and remember: then is there any that will receive admonition?
22.shakir: And certainly We have made the Quran easy for remembrance, but is there anyone who will mind?
22.muhammad_sarwar: We have made the Quran easy to understand, but is there anyone who would pay attention?
22.mohsin_khan: And We have indeed made the Quran easy to understand and remember, then is there any that will remember (or receive admonition)?
22.arberry: Now We have made the Koran easy for Remembrance. Is there any that will remember?

23.muhammad_sarwar: The people of Thamud rejected Our warnings.
23.arberry: Thamood cried lies to the warnings

24.sahih_international: And said, "Is it one human being among us that we should follow? Indeed, we would then be in error and madness.
24.pickthall: For they said; Is it a mortal man, alone among us, that we are to follow? Then indeed we should fall into error and madness.
24.yusuf_ali: For they said: "What! a man! a Solitary one from among ourselves! shall we follow such a one? Truly should we then be straying in mind, and mad!
24.shakir: So they said: What! a single mortal from among us! Shall we follow him? Most surely we shall in that case be in sure error and distress:
24.muhammad_sarwar: They said, "Should we follow only one person among us. We shall be clearly in error and in trouble (if we do so).
24.mohsin_khan: For they said: "A man! Alone from among us, that we are to follow? Truly, then we should be in error and distress or madness!"
24.arberry: and said, 'What, shall we follow a mortal, one out of ourselves? Then indeed we should be in error and insanity!

25.sahih_international: Has the message been sent down upon him from among us? Rather, he is an insolent liar."
25.pickthall: Hath the remembrance been given unto him alone among us? Nay, but he is a rash liar.
25.yusuf_ali: "Is it that the Message is sent to him, of all people amongst us? Nay, he is a liar, an insolent one!"
25.shakir: Has the reminder been made to light upon him from among us? Nay! he is an insolent liar!
25.muhammad_sarwar: How is it that he has received guidance? In fact, he is the most untruthfull and arrogant person".
25.mohsin_khan: "Is it that the Reminder is sent to him [Prophet Salih (Saleh)] alone from among us? Nay, he is an insolent liar!"
25.arberry: Has the Reminder been cast upon him alone among us? Nay, rather he is an impudent liar.'

26.sahih_international: They will know tomorrow who is the insolent liar.
26.pickthall: (Unto their warner it was said): To-morrow they will know who is the rash liar.
26.yusuf_ali: Ah! they will know on the morrow, which is the liar, the insolent one!
26.shakir: Tomorrow shall they know who is the liar, the insolent one.
26.muhammad_sarwar: (We told Salih), "Tomorrow they will know who is the most arrogant liar.
26.mohsin_khan: Tomorrow they will come to know, who is the liar, the insolent one!
26.arberry: 'They shall surely know tomorrow who is the impudent liar.

27.sahih_international: Indeed, We are sending the she-camel as trial for them, so watch them and be patient.
27.pickthall: Lo! We are sending the she-camel as a test for them; so watch them and have patience;
27.yusuf_ali: For We will send the she-camel by way of trial for them. So watch them, (O Salih), and possess thyself in patience!
27.shakir: Surely We are going to send the she-camel as a trial for them; therefore watch them and have patience.
27.muhammad_sarwar: We are sending the she-camel to them to test them. So watch them and be patient.
27.mohsin_khan: Verily, We are sending the she-camel as a test for them. So watch them [O Salih (Saleh)], and be patient!
27.arberry: They shall send the She-camel as a trial for them; so watch thou them and keep patience.

28.sahih_international: And inform them that the water is shared between them, each [day of] drink attended [by turn].
28.pickthall: And inform them that the water is to be shared between (her and) them. Every drinking will be witnessed.
28.yusuf_ali: And tell them that the water is to be divided between them: Each one's right to drink being brought forward (by suitable turns).
28.shakir: And inform them that the water is shared between them; every share of the water shall be regulated.
28.muhammad_sarwar: Tell them that each one of them has the right to have a certain share of water".
28.mohsin_khan: And inform them that the water is to be shared between (her and) them. Each one's right to drink being established (by turns).
28.arberry: And tell them that the water is to be divided between them, each drink for each in turn.

29.sahih_international: But they called their companion, and he dared and hamstrung [her].
29.pickthall: But they call their comrade and he took and hamstrung (her).
29.yusuf_ali: But they called to their companion, and he took a sword in hand, and hamstrung (her).
29.shakir: But they called their companion, so he took (the sword) and slew (her).
29.muhammad_sarwar: They called together their companions and agreed to slay the she-camel.
29.mohsin_khan: But they called their comrade and he took (a sword) and killed (her).
29.arberry: Then they called their comrade, and he took in hand, and hamstrung her.

30.sahih_international: And how [severe] were My punishment and warning.
30.pickthall: Then see how (dreadful) was My punishment after My warnings!
30.yusuf_ali: Ah! how (terrible) was My Penalty and My Warning!
30.shakir: How (great) was then My punishment and My warning!
30.muhammad_sarwar: How terrible was My punishment and warning.
30.mohsin_khan: Then, how (terrible) was My Torment and My Warnings?
30.arberry: How then were My chastisement and My warnings?

31.sahih_international: Indeed, We sent upon them one blast from the sky, and they became like the dry twig fragments of an [animal] pen.
31.pickthall: Lo! We sent upon them one Shout, and they became as the dry twigs (rejected by) the builder of a cattle-fold.
31.yusuf_ali: For We sent against them a single Mighty Blast, and they became like the dry stubble used by one who pens cattle.
31.shakir: Surely We sent upon them a single cry, so they were like the dry fragments of trees which the maker of an enclosure collects.
31.muhammad_sarwar: We sent upon them a single blast of sound and they were left like hay to be used by the cattle.
31.mohsin_khan: Verily, We sent against them a single Saihah (torment - awful cry, etc.), and they became like the dry stubble of a fold-builder.
31.arberry: We loosed against them one Cry, and they were as the wattles of a pen-builder.

32.sahih_international: And We have certainly made the Qur'an easy for remembrance, so is there any who will remember?
32.pickthall: And in truth We have made the Qur'an easy to remember; but is there any that remembereth?
32.yusuf_ali: And We have indeed made the Qur'an easy to understand and remember: then is there any that will receive admonition?
32.shakir: And certainly We have made the Quran easy for remembrance, but is there anyone who will mind?
32.muhammad_sarwar: We made the Quran easy to understand, but is there anyone who would take heed?
32.mohsin_khan: And indeed, We have made the Quran easy to understand and remember, then is there any that will remember (or receive admonition)?
32.arberry: Now We have made the Koran easy for Remembrance. Is there any that will remember?

33.sahih_international: The people of Lot denied the warning.
33.pickthall: The folk of Lot rejected warnings.
33.yusuf_ali: The people of Lut rejected (his) warning.
33.shakir: The people of Lut treated the warning. as a lie.
33.muhammad_sarwar: The people of Lot rejected Our warning.
33.mohsin_khan: The people of Lout (Lot) belied the warnings.
33.arberry: The people of Lot cried lies to the warnings.

34.sahih_international: Indeed, We sent upon them a storm of stones, except the family of Lot - We saved them before dawn
34.pickthall: Lo! We sent a storm of stones upon them (all) save the family of Lot, whom We rescued in the last watch of the night,
34.yusuf_ali: We sent against them a violent Tornado with showers of stones, (which destroyed them), except Lut's household: them We delivered by early Dawn,-
34.shakir: Surely We sent upon them a stonestorm, except Lut's followers; We saved them a little before daybreak,
34.muhammad_sarwar: We sent down upon them a violent sandstorm (which destroyed them all) except for the family of Lot, whom We saved in the early morning by Our favor.
34.mohsin_khan: Verily, We sent against them a violent storm of stones (which destroyed them all), except the family of Lout (Lot), whom We saved in last hour of the night,
34.arberry: We loosed against them a squall of pebbles except the folk of Lot; We delivered them at the dawn --

35.sahih_international: As favor from us. Thus do We reward he who is grateful.
35.pickthall: As grace from Us. Thus We reward him who giveth thanks.
35.yusuf_ali: As a Grace from Us: thus do We reward those who give thanks.
35.shakir: A favor from Us; thus do We reward him who gives thanks.
35.muhammad_sarwar: Thus do We recompense the grateful ones.
35.mohsin_khan: As a Favour from Us, thus do We reward him who gives thanks (by obeying Us).
35.arberry: a blessing from Us; even so We recompense him who is thankful.

36.sahih_international: And he had already warned them of Our assault, but they disputed the warning.
36.pickthall: And he indeed had warned them of Our blow, but they did doubt the warnings.
36.yusuf_ali: And (Lut) did warn them of Our Punishment, but they disputed about the Warning.
36.shakir: And certainly he warned them of Our violent seizure, but they obstinately disputed the warning.
36.muhammad_sarwar: Lot warned them against Our torment, but they persistently disputed it.
36.mohsin_khan: And he [Lout (Lot)] indeed had warned them of Our Grasp, but they did doubt the warnings!
36.arberry: He had warned them of Our assault, but they disputed the warnings.

37.sahih_international: And they had demanded from him his guests, but We obliterated their eyes, [saying], "Taste My punishment and warning."
37.pickthall: They even asked of him his guests for an ill purpose. Then We blinded their eyes (and said): Taste now My punishment after My warnings!
37.yusuf_ali: And they even sought to snatch away his guests from him, but We blinded their eyes. (They heard:) "Now taste ye My Wrath and My Warning."
37.shakir: And certainly they endeavored to turn him from his guests, but We blinded their eyes; so taste My chastisement and My warning.
37.muhammad_sarwar: They demanded that he turn over his guests to them.
37.mohsin_khan: And they indeed sought to shame his guest (by asking to commit sodomy with them). So We blinded their eyes, "Then taste you My Torment and My Warnings."
37.arberry: Even his guests they had solicited of him; so We obliterated their eyes, saying, 'Taste now My chastisement and My warnings!'

38.sahih_international: And there came upon them by morning an abiding punishment.
38.pickthall: And in truth the punishment decreed befell them early in the morning.
38.yusuf_ali: Early on the morrow an abiding Punishment seized them:
38.shakir: And certainly a lasting chastisement overtook them in the morning.
38.muhammad_sarwar: We struck their faces, blinded them and said, "Suffer Our torment of which you were warned".
38.mohsin_khan: And verily, an abiding torment seized them early in the morning.
38.arberry: In the morning early there came upon them a settled chastisement:

39.sahih_international: So taste My punishment and warning.
39.pickthall: Now taste My punishment after My warnings!
39.yusuf_ali: "So taste ye My Wrath and My Warning."
39.shakir: So taste My chastisement and My warning.
39.muhammad_sarwar: One early morning Our torment brought upon them utter destruction. We said, "Suffer Our torment of which you were warned".
39.mohsin_khan: "Then taste you My Torment and My Warnings."
39.arberry: 'Taste now My chastisement and My warnings!'

40.sahih_international: And We have certainly made the Qur'an easy for remembrance, so is there any who will remember?
40.pickthall: And in truth We have made the Qur'an easy to remember; but is there any that remembereth?
40.yusuf_ali: And We have indeed made the Qur'an easy to understand and remember: then is there any that will receive admonition?
40.shakir: And certainly We have made the Quran easy for remembrance, but is there anyone who will mind?
40.muhammad_sarwar: We have made the Quran easy to understand, but is there anyone who would pay attention?
40.mohsin_khan: And indeed, We have made the Quran easy to understand and remember, then is there any that will remember (or receive admonition)?
40.arberry: Now We have made the Koran easy for Remembrance. Is there any that will remember?

41.sahih_international: And there certainly came to the people of Pharaoh warning.
41.pickthall: And warnings came in truth unto the house of Pharaoh
41.yusuf_ali: To the People of Pharaoh, too, aforetime, came Warners (from Allah).
41.shakir: And certainly the warning came to Firon's people.
41.muhammad_sarwar: The Pharaoh and his people had also received Our warning,
41.mohsin_khan: And indeed, warnings came to the people of Fir'aun (Pharaoh) [through Musa (Moses) and Harun (Aaron)].
41.arberry: The warnings came also to Pharaoh's folk.

42.sahih_international: They denied Our signs, all of them, so We seized them with a seizure of one Exalted in Might and Perfect in Ability.
42.pickthall: Who denied Our revelations, every one. Therefore We grasped them with the grasp of the Mighty, the Powerful.
42.yusuf_ali: The (people) rejected all Our Signs; but We seized them with such Penalty (as comes) from One Exalted in Power, able to carry out His Will.
42.shakir: They rejected all Our communications, so We overtook them after the manner of a Mighty, Powerful One.
42.muhammad_sarwar: but they rejected all Our miracles. So We seized them in the way that a Majestic and All-powerful One would.
42.mohsin_khan: (They) belied all Our Signs, so We seized them with a Seizure of the All-Mighty, All-Capable to carry out what he Will (Omnipotent).
42.arberry: They cried lies to Our signs, all of them, so We seized them with the seizing of One mighty, omnipotent.

43.sahih_international: Are your disbelievers better than those [former ones], or have you immunity in the scripture?
43.pickthall: Are your disbelievers better than those, or have ye some immunity in the scriptures?
43.yusuf_ali: Are your Unbelievers, (O Quraish), better than they? Or have ye an immunity in the Sacred Books?
43.shakir: Are the unbelievers of yours better than these, or is there an exemption for you in the scriptures?
43.muhammad_sarwar: Are you disbelievers mightier than those of the nations which We destroyed before or have you received amnesty through the ancient Scriptures?
43.mohsin_khan: Are your disbelievers (O Quraish!) better than these [nations of Nuh (Noah), Lout (Lot), Salih (Saleh), and the people of Fir'aun (Pharaoh), etc., who were destroyed)? Or have you an immunity (against Our Torment) in the Divine Scriptures?
43.arberry: What, are your unbelievers better than those? Or have you an immunity in the Scrolls?

44.sahih_international: Or do they say, "We are an assembly supporting [each other]"?
44.pickthall: Or say they: We are a host victorious?
44.yusuf_ali: Or do they say: "We acting together can defend ourselves"?
44.shakir: Or do they say: We are a host allied together to help each other?
44.muhammad_sarwar: Do they say, "We shall be victorious because we are united?"
44.mohsin_khan: Or do they say: "We are a great multitude, and we shall be victorious?"
44.arberry: Or do they say, 'We are a congregation that shall be succoured?'

45.sahih_international: [Their] assembly will be defeated, and they will turn their backs [in retreat].
45.pickthall: The hosts will all be routed and will turn and flee.
45.yusuf_ali: Soon will their multitude be put to flight, and they will show their backs.
45.shakir: Soon shall the hosts be routed, and they shall turn (their) backs.
45.muhammad_sarwar: (Let them know that) this united group will soon run away in defeat.
45.mohsin_khan: Their multitude will be put to flight, and they will show their backs.
45.arberry: Certainly the host shall be routed, and turn their backs.

46.sahih_international: But the Hour is their appointment [for due punishment], and the Hour is more disastrous and more bitter.
46.pickthall: Nay, but the Hour (of doom) is their appointed tryst, and the Hour will be more wretched and more bitter (than their earthly failure).
46.yusuf_ali: Nay, the Hour (of Judgment) is the time promised them (for their full recompense): And that Hour will be most grievous and most bitter.
46.shakir: Nay, the hour is their promised time, and the hour shall be most grievous and bitter.
46.muhammad_sarwar: In fact, the Hour of Doom is the time for them to suffer. The suffering of this hour is the most calamitous and the most bitter (of all suffering).
46.mohsin_khan: Nay, but the Hour is their appointed time (for their full recompense), and the Hour will be more grievous and more bitter.
46.arberry: Nay, but the Hour is their tryst, and the Hour is very calamitous and bitter.

47.sahih_international: Indeed, the criminals are in error and madness.
47.pickthall: Lo! the guilty are in error and madness.
47.yusuf_ali: Truly those in sin are the ones straying in mind, and mad.
47.shakir: Surely the guilty are in error and distress.
47.muhammad_sarwar: The sinful ones will face the destructive torment of hell
47.mohsin_khan: Verily, the Mujrimun (polytheists, disbelievers, sinners, criminals, etc.) are in error (in this world) and will burn (in the Hell-fire in the Hereafter).
47.arberry: Surely the sinners are in error and insanity!

48.sahih_international: The Day they are dragged into the Fire on their faces [it will be said], "Taste the touch of Saqar."
48.pickthall: On the day when they are dragged into the Fire upon their faces (it is said unto them): Feel the touch of hell.
48.yusuf_ali: The Day they will be dragged through the Fire on their faces, (they will hear:) "Taste ye the touch of Hell!"
48.shakir: On the day when they shall be dragged upon their faces into the fire; taste the touch of hell.
48.muhammad_sarwar: when they will be dragged on their faces into the fire and will be told, "Feel the touch of hell".
48.mohsin_khan: The Day they will be dragged in the Fire on their faces (it will be said to them): "Taste you the touch of Hell!"
48.arberry: The day when they are dragged on their faces into the Fire: 'Taste now the touch of Sakar!'

49.sahih_international: Indeed, all things We created with predestination.
49.pickthall: Lo! We have created every thing by measure.
49.yusuf_ali: Verily, all things have We created in proportion and measure.
49.shakir: Surely We have created everything according to a measure.
49.muhammad_sarwar: We have created everything to fulfill a certain purpose.
49.mohsin_khan: Verily, We have created all things with Qadar (Divine Preordainments of all things before their creation, as written in the Book of Decrees Al-Lauh Al-Mahfuz).
49.arberry: Surely We have created everything in measure.

50.sahih_international: And Our command is but one, like a glance of the eye.
50.pickthall: And Our commandment is but one (commandment), as the twinkling of an eye.
50.yusuf_ali: And Our Command is but a single (Act),- like the twinkling of an eye.
50.shakir: And Our command is but one, as the twinkling of an eye.
50.muhammad_sarwar: It takes only a single command from Us (to bring the Day of Judgment) and that can be achieved within the twinkling of an eye.
50.mohsin_khan: And Our Commandment is but one, as the twinkling of an eye.
50.arberry: Our commandment is but one word, as the twinkling of an eye.

51.sahih_international: And We have already destroyed your kinds, so is there any who will remember?
51.pickthall: And verily We have destroyed your fellows; but is there any that remembereth?
51.yusuf_ali: And (oft) in the past, have We destroyed gangs like unto you: then is there any that will receive admonition?
51.shakir: And certainly We have already destroyed the likes of you, but is there anyone who will mind?
51.muhammad_sarwar: We destroyed many people like you (disbelievers) but is there anyone who would take heed (of Our warning)?
51.mohsin_khan: And indeed, We have destroyed your likes, then is there any that will remember (or receive admonition)?
51.arberry: We have destroyed the likes of you; is there any that will remember?

52.sahih_international: And everything they did is in written records.
52.pickthall: And every thing they did is in the scriptures,
52.yusuf_ali: All that they do is noted in (their) Books (of Deeds):
52.shakir: And everything they have done is in the writings.
52.muhammad_sarwar: Whatever they have done has been recorded in the Books (records of the deeds).
52.mohsin_khan: And each and everything they have done is noted in (their) Records (of deeds).
52.arberry: Every thing that they have done is in the Scrolls,

53.sahih_international: And every small and great [thing] is inscribed.
53.pickthall: And every small and great thing is recorded.
53.yusuf_ali: Every matter, small and great, is on record.
53.shakir: And everything small and great is written down.
53.muhammad_sarwar: Every small or great deed is written down.
53.mohsin_khan: And everything, small and big is written (in Al-Lauh Al-Mahfuz already beforehand i.e. before it befalls, or is done by its doer) (See the Quran V. 57:22).
53.arberry: and everything, great and small, is inscribed.

54.sahih_international: Indeed, the righteous will be among gardens and rivers,
54.pickthall: Lo! the righteous will dwell among gardens and rivers,
54.yusuf_ali: As to the Righteous, they will be in the midst of Gardens and Rivers,
54.shakir: Surely those who guard (against evil) shall be in gardens and rivers,
54.muhammad_sarwar: The pious ones will live in Paradise wherein streams flow,
54.mohsin_khan: Verily, The Muttaqun (pious), will be in the midst of Gardens and Rivers (Paradise).
54.arberry: Surely the godfearing shall dwell amid gardens and a river

55.sahih_international: In a seat of honor near a Sovereign, Perfect in Ability.
55.pickthall: Firmly established in the favour of a Mighty King.
55.yusuf_ali: In an Assembly of Truth, in the Presence of a Sovereign Omnipotent.
55.shakir: In the seat of honor with a most Powerful King.
55.muhammad_sarwar: honorably seated in the presence of the All-dominant King.
55.mohsin_khan: In a seat of truth (i.e. Paradise), near the Omnipotent King (Allah, the All-Blessed, the Most High, the Owner of Majesty and Honour).
55.arberry: in a sure abode, in the presence of a King Omnipotent.
